title: What If All the Permafrost Thawed?

scenes.text: What if all the permafrost thawed? The ground itself would start to collapse.
Permafrost covers about a quarter of the Northern Hemisphere's land. Some of it has been frozen for hundreds of thousands of years.
When the ice in the soil melts, the ground slumps. Trees tilt, roads buckle, and bridges sink.
Frozen plants have been locked in that soil since the last ice age. Thaw lets microbes start eating them.
As they rot, they release carbon dioxide and methane. Estimates say the soil holds 1,400 to 1,670 billion tons of carbon.
One study expects a third to two thirds of it to vanish by 2200, releasing carbon equal to half of all industrial emissions.

description:
What if all the permafrost thawed?
It holds more carbon than the whole atmosphere, and thaw is already tilting trees and sinking bridges in Alaska.
What should we run through next?
